title: Cover before you test
hook: You've just read three cards, answers showing. Covered, how many will you get?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that you only find out whether you can recall an answer if it is hidden while you try; with it in view you recognise it instead of remembering it

misconception: Rereading a card with the answer showing tests what you know.
objective: Perform a closed-answer check before using feedback.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: You've just read three cards, answers showing. Covered, how many will you get? You look at 'cue → answer' cards with the answers showing and get 3 of 3. Cover the answers: how many can you give? Options: 3: I just saw them / Can't tell until you try / 0. Correct option: Can't tell until you try. claims.text: Covering the answer removes the direct reading route. This reconstruction records one attempt, not a long-term memory score.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Stage: the card (bell → lake, kite → plum, leaf → door) shows at the prediction and is covered after it (bell → ?, kite → ?, leaf → ?). Each answer box starts empty and cycles through fixed choices (leaf: door, dock, plum; bell: lane, lake, door; kite: plum, pear, lake). Pressing each box once gives: Covered 2 of 3. The readout “Answers showing 3/3” stands for the check made with everything in view. Reveal sentences: With the answers showing, all three cards read right. Nothing missed this time, and only the covered try could tell you that.

recall.question: You want to check that you know the Spanish words on a two-column list. Which check makes you retrieve each word?
options: Read down both columns slowly, twice
Fold over the Spanish column, then say each word
Tick each Spanish word you recognise on sight
recall.why: Hiding the answer removes the reading route, so you have to produce it; rereading and recognising still show it to you.
